text_verbatim: The Commission may, for the purpose of ensuring continuity of telecommunication services in an emergency, issue directions to an operator regarding the operation, restoration and prioritisation of its telecommunication system, and the operator shall comply with such directions.

The Government may, in the interest of the security of the State or public order, direct the suspension or interception of telecommunication services, and any such direction shall be issued by the authority empowered by the Government for that purpose.

An operator shall not provide or alter international roaming arrangements, including arrangements with operators of a neighbouring country, except with the prior written approval of the Commission, and any request for such approval shall be processed in accordance with the Commission's standard timelines.

The Cyclone Preparedness Programme shall disseminate cyclone warning signals issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department to coastal communities through its network of volunteers using megaphones, flags and sirens, in Bengali, and shall continue dissemination until the danger signal is withdrawn.

The National Disaster Management Council shall approve national disaster management policies and plans, and the Department of Disaster Management shall coordinate the dissemination of early warnings for impending disasters to the population of the areas likely to be affected, in Bengali.

On receipt of an early warning of an impending disaster, the Deputy Commissioner of the district concerned shall activate the district disaster management committee and shall cause the warning to be disseminated to the inhabitants of the areas likely to be affected through all available means without delay.

The State Executive Committee shall give directions to any department of the Government of the State or any other authority or body in the State regarding actions to be taken in response to any threatening disaster situation or disaster, and shall advise the State Government regarding all financial matters in relation to disaster management.

The District Authority shall ensure that communication systems are in order and that disaster management drills are carried out periodically, and shall, in the event of a disaster, provide information to the State Authority relating to different aspects of disaster management.

text_raw: 6. (1) The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of her personal data for the specified purpose and be limited to such personal data as is necessary for such specified purpose. Illustration. X, an individual, downloads Y, a telemedicine app. Y requests the consent of X for (i) the processing of her personal data for making available telemedicine services, and (ii) accessing her mobile phone contact list, and X signifies her consent to both. Since phone contact list is not necessary for making available telemedicine services, her consent shall be limited to the processing of her personal data for making available telemedicine services. (2) Any part of consent referred in sub-section (1) which constitutes an infringement of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder or any other law for the time being in force shall be invalid to the extent of such infringement. Illustration. X, an individual, buys an insurance policy using the mobile app or website of Y, an insurer. She gives to Y her consent for (i) the processing of her personal data by Y for the purpose of issuing the policy, and (ii) waiving her right to file a complaint to the Data Protection Board of India. Part (ii) of the consent, relating to waiver of her right to file a complaint, shall be invalid. (3) Every request for consent under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall be presented to the Data Principal in a clear and plain language, giving her the option to access such request in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution and providing the contact details of a Data Protection Officer, where applicable, or of any other person authorised by the Data Fiduciary to respond to any communication from the Data Principal for the purpose of exercise of her rights under the provisions of this Act. (4) Where consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing of personal data, such Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw her consent at any time, with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given. (5) The consequences of the withdrawal referred to in sub-section (4) shall be borne by the Data Principal, and such withdrawal shall not affect the legality of processing of the personal data based on consent before its withdrawal. Illustration. X, an individual, is the user of an online shopping app or website operated by Y, an e-commerce service provider. (1) A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor. (2) A Data Fiduciary may engage, appoint, use or otherwise involve a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf for any activity related to offering of goods or services to Data Principals only under a valid contract. (3) Where personal data processed by a Data Fiduciary is likely to be— (a) used to make a decision that affects the Data Principal; or (b) disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, the Data Fiduciary processing such personal data shall ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency. (4) A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. (5) A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach. (6) In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be prescribed. (7) A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law for the time being in force,— (a) erase personal data, upon the Data Principal withdrawing her consent or as General obligations of Data Fiduciary. X gives her consent to Y for the processing of her personal data for selling her used car. The online marketplace helps conclude the sale. Y shall no longer retain her personal data. (II) X, an individual, decides to close her savings account with Y, a bank. Y is required by law applicable to banks to maintain the record of the identity of its clients for a period of ten years beyond closing of accounts. Since retention is necessary for compliance with law, Y shall retain X’s personal data for the said period. text_verbatim: The India Meteorological Department issues cyclone warnings in four stages: Pre-Cyclone Watch, Cyclone Alert, Cyclone Warning, and Post-Landfall Outlook, addressed to the State Governments and disaster management authorities of the areas likely to be affected, with the Cyclone Warning stage issued at least twenty-four hours before expected commencement of adverse weather.

Every order issued directing suspension of telecommunication services shall contain reasons for such direction, shall specify the area and duration of suspension, and a copy of such order shall be forwarded to the concerned Review Committee not later than the next working day.

Any direction for suspension of telecommunication services shall not remain in operation for more than fifteen days at a time, and a fresh order shall be required to continue the suspension beyond that period.

The Review Committee shall meet within five working days of the issue of a direction for suspension of telecommunication services and shall record its findings on whether the direction is in accordance with the governing provisions of law.

The authorised entity shall designate a nodal officer in each licensed service area to receive and handle directions for suspension of telecommunication services, and no direction shall be acted upon unless it is received through the designated nodal officer channel.

(1) Any facility provider may submit an application to a public entity under for whose ownership, control or management, the public property is vested, to seek telecommunication permissions for right of way for telecommunication network under, over, along, across, network in public property. in or upon such public property. (2) On receipt of an application from a facility provider under sub-section (1), the public entity shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (4), grant permission for all or any of the following acts, namely:— (a) survey such property for the purpose of assessing the feasibility for establishing telecommunication network; or (b) enter the property from time to time to establish, operate, maintain, repair, replace, augment, remove or relocate any telecommunication network. (3) The public entity shall grant permission under sub-section (2) in an expeditious manner and within such timelines as may be prescribed, and subject to such administrative expenses and compensation for right of way, which shall not exceed such amount as may be prescribed. (4) Any rejection of an application under sub-section (1) shall be based on reasonable grounds to be recorded in writing. (5) The facility provider shall do as little damage as possible to the public property, and ensure that the functionality and continuity of operations over such public property is not adversely affected, while undertaking any of the activities for which permission has been granted under sub-section (2). (6) If any damage is caused to the property, the facility provider shall, at the option of the public entity, either,— (a) restore such property to its state as existed prior to the undertaking of such activities; or (b) pay compensation for such damage as may be mutually agreed. (7) The provisions of this section shall be applicable to any public property vested for such projects or class of projects as notified by the Central Government, in respect of which, applications under sub-section (1) shall be made to the public entity granting the concession, contract or permission for such projects. instrument: GSMA guidance on mobile network operator disaster response
text_verbatim: Where national regulation permits, operators may implement disaster roaming so that subscribers of an operator whose radio access network is unavailable in a disaster-affected area can register on a surviving network, subject to pre-agreed technical arrangements and a defined trigger and termination condition.

instrument: Constitution of the International Telecommunication Union
text_verbatim: International telecommunication services must accord absolute priority to all telecommunications concerning safety of life at sea, on land, in the air or in outer space, as well as to epidemiological telecommunications of exceptional urgency of the World Health Organization.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation E.106, International Emergency Preference Scheme for disaster relief operations
text_verbatim: The International Emergency Preference Scheme provides for priority treatment of calls made by authorised personnel engaged in disaster relief operations, including priority in call set-up and preferential access to network resources, to be applied by network operators on the basis of authorisation granted by the responsible national authority.

instrument: ITU-D Guidelines for National Emergency Telecommunication Plans (2020)
text_verbatim: The ITU guidelines set out how a country should develop a national emergency telecommunication plan covering preparedness, response and recovery for telecommunication networks, and reflect the ITU objective that every country have such a plan in place. Cited as the global benchmark against which a national SOP is compared.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Q.3057 (signature-based calling party identity authentication)
text_verbatim: ITU-T standardises certificate-based authentication of calling party identity in signalling, providing a signed-identity mechanism and the supporting protocol and certificate-management procedures. Cited to show that ITU already standardises cryptographically signed identity in telecommunication signalling, while no analogous mechanism exists for authenticating a government direction issued to an operator.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation X.1303, Common Alerting Protocol (CAP 1.1)
text_verbatim: The Common Alerting Protocol provides an open, non-proprietary digital message format for all types of alerts and notifications, specifying an alert message structure with alert, info, resource and area blocks, where the info block carries the language, category, urgency, severity and certainty of the alert and the area block carries the geographic scope.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Y.3172, Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
text_verbatim: The machine learning pipeline is a set of logical nodes, each with specific functionalities, that can be combined to form a machine learning application. The nodes comprise SRC (source), C (collector), PP (pre-processor), M (model), P (policy), D (distributor) and SINK, where the policy node applies constraints on the output of the model node before it is applied to the network.

instrument: ITU-T Recommendation Y.3173, Framework for evaluating intelligence levels of future networks including IMT-2020
text_verbatim: The framework evaluates the intelligence level of a network across dimensions including monitoring, analysis, decision and execution, where higher levels correspond to a greater degree of autonomous decision making and lower levels retain human involvement in the decision and execution steps.

instrument: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030
text_verbatim: To invest in, develop, maintain and strengthen people-centred multi-hazard, multisectoral forecasting and early warning systems, disaster risk and emergency communications mechanisms, social technologies and hazard-monitoring telecommunications systems, and to develop such systems through a participatory process, tailoring them to the needs of users, including social and cultural requirements, in particular gender.

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: The States Parties shall cooperate among themselves and with non-State entities and intergovernmental organizations to facilitate the use of telecommunication resources for disaster mitigation and relief, including the deployment of terrestrial and satellite telecommunication equipment to predict, monitor and provide information concerning natural hazards and disasters. Party status of individual States must be verified on the UN Treaty Collection before being encoded in a policy pack (see spec section 14).

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: A State Party requiring telecommunication assistance for disaster mitigation and relief may request such assistance from any other State Party, and the requested State Party shall promptly determine and notify the requesting State Party whether it will render the assistance requested, directly or otherwise, and the scope of and terms on which such assistance might be rendered.

instrument: Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations, 1998
text_verbatim: States Parties shall, where possible and in conformity with their national law, reduce or remove regulatory barriers to the use of telecommunication resources for disaster mitigation and relief, including barriers relating to the licensing of the use of allocated frequencies, restrictions on the import of equipment, limitations on the movement of humanitarian teams, and restrictions on roaming and the use of telecommunication resources across borders.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: Facilities-based mobile wireless providers shall, when the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative is triggered, provide reasonable roaming under disaster arrangements to requesting providers where technically feasible, so that subscribers of a provider whose network is impaired in the affected area can obtain service on another provider's network.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: Participating providers shall engage in mutual aid during emergencies, including enhanced municipal preparedness and restoration coordination, and shall provide a single point of contact for public safety entities in the affected area for the duration of the event.

instrument: 47 CFR 4.17 — Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (United States)
text_verbatim: The obligations of the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative are triggered automatically upon activation of the Disaster Information Reporting System for an area, without the need for a separate order from the Commission directed at each provider.

instrument: 47 CFR Part 4 -- Disruptions to Communications (United States)
text_verbatim: Wireless service providers shall submit electronically a notification to the Commission within 120 minutes of discovering an outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility, and shall submit an initial outage report within 72 hours and a final report within 30 days of discovering the outage.

instrument: FCC Disaster Information Reporting System (United States)
text_verbatim: When the Disaster Information Reporting System is activated for a geographic area, communications providers in that area are directed to report the operational status of their infrastructure, including cell sites out of service and switches down, on a daily basis for the duration of the activation.

instrument: FCC Wireless Emergency Alerts rules (United States)
text_verbatim: Participating Commercial Mobile Service providers shall support transmission of Wireless Emergency Alerts in English and Spanish, and shall transmit alerts received from the Alert Gateway to the geographic area specified by the alert originator.
